title: Employee Scheduling Problem v4.0 - declarative form
description: The problem as SISQUAL's exporter produces it, spelled canonically. JSON carries the structure; four CSVs carry the matrices (three demand grains plus the per-employee-per-day input). v4.0 keys coverage on a two-dimensional (tableName, tableValue) coordinate rather than v3.0's single competency code, and re-admits the priorityHierarchy and constraints blocks that v3.0 had cut. Standalone: this file does not reference any other schema. Symbols in square brackets refer to MathematicalDefinition7. SISQUAL's raw emission does NOT validate against this file - run src/schema_v4/sisqual_adapt.py first; docs/DIALECT.md lists every difference.

minutes.description: Minutes from 00:00. Values at or past 1440 express times after midnight.

competenceLevel.description: Proficiency in a (tableName, tableValue) competency [l_ws]. LEVEL 1 IS THE HIGHEST; larger numbers are progressively lower. A priorityHierarchy entry whose minAbilityLevel is 1 therefore reaches that competency's most senior workers.

problemId.description: Identity of the problem. SISQUAL emits <RosterCode>_<Month>_<Year>, e.g. C2_January_2026; a result's RosterCode must be this id's leading segment.

source.description: Who produced the bundle. SISQUAL's exporter writes "SISQUAL".

rosterCode.description: SISQUAL's RosterCode (the "quadro"), carried explicitly rather than parsed back out of problemId. The adapter fills this in.

slotMinutes.description: Width of one timeslot [T]. Must divide 1440. SISQUAL emits 30.

end.description: Inclusive. schedule_input.csv carries one date column per day in start..end.

holidays.description: Days the enterprise may give their own demand rows. Marking a holiday does NOT make anyone unavailable. SISQUAL emits this as inpUAHolidaysCollection; the adapter renames it.

hasEve.description: The preceding day is this holiday's eve and may carry its own demand. The eve's date is this date minus one, so only its existence needs stating.

definitions.description: The contract catalogue. May be empty - SISQUAL's July bundle emitted [] while every employee referenced a contract, which the validator reports as a dangling reference.

name.description: SISQUAL's pattern is "[<CC>] <N>h Semanais - <Full-Time|Part-Time>", where N is WEEKLY hours. Do not derive workMinutesPerDay from it.

workMinutesPerDay.description: Length of one working day in minutes [H_w]. SISQUAL's TotalDailyMinutes. Note the unit clash: schedule_input.csv states the same quantity in HOURS.

id.description: Employee identifier [w]. A string even when it looks numeric.

contractAssignments.description: Date-ranged contract membership. SISQUAL misspells the key as contractAssigments; the adapter corrects it.

end.description: null means open-ended. SISQUAL writes the sentinel 9999-12-31; the adapter converts it to null.

competencyAssignments.description: Date-ranged, levelled competencies [S_w]. May be empty - Cenario 1 ships with no competencies at all.

tableName.description: Coverage dimension. Must appear in demand.dimensions[].

tableValue.description: Value within that dimension. The pair must appear in demand.dimensions[].

demand.description: Coverage wanted, split across three CSVs by grain. Only the periods file carries data in every bundle seen so far, but all three pointers are required so a package is self-describing.

dimensions.description: The catalogue of (tableName, tableValue) coordinates this problem uses - the v4 replacement for v3.0's demand.organizationalUnits.competencies[]. Required, because it is the only thing that makes tableName checkable: SISQUAL's bundles declare no catalogue, and the three places the pairs appear disagree on the dimension name. The adapter synthesises it.

dataFileDays.description: CSV of whole-day WORKLOAD demand, in minutes - SISQUAL's InpServiceLevelByDays. Different unit from the other two. Resolved relative to this JSON file.

dataFilePeriods.description: CSV of HEADCOUNT demand per time window - SISQUAL's InpServiceLevelByPeriods. Byte-identical header to the days file; only this key tells them apart.

dataFileShifts.description: CSV of HEADCOUNT demand per shift type - SISQUAL's InpServiceLevelByShifts. Adds a workPeriod column.

scheduleInput.description: Per-employee-per-day requirements, held as a CSV matrix (one row per employee, one column per date).

dataFile.description: Resolved relative to this JSON file. Numeric cells are HOURS in v4.0 - see docs/FORMAT.md.

dayOffCodes.description: The palette of non-working cell codes, keyed by the code itself. Every non-numeric cell in the CSV must be a key here. Keys may be non-ASCII (SISQUAL uses "Fer" with an accent).

kind.description: preferable [D_wk] is soft - the solver may schedule over it at a penalty. unavailable [U_wk] is hard - no assignment permitted. SISQUAL capitalises both; the adapter lowercases them.

schedules.description: The ScheduleCode catalogue - the menu a result must pick from. SISQUAL specifies it as InpScheduleUsedCollection but does not export it; it arrived as a spreadsheet. Optional, because two of the three bundles have no copy.

dataFile.description: CSV of code,description,scheduleWeightMinutes,startMin,endMin. Resolved relative to this JSON file.

priorityHierarchy.description: Fill order and the alarm-table settings that drive it - SISQUAL's priorityHierachy (sic), a nine-field projection of InpGenerationRules. Lower rank is filled first. Absent from the July bundle, so optional.

rank.description: Fill order; lower is filled first. Must be unique. Ordering follows rank, not array position.

label.description: UI caption. SISQUAL emits Portuguese (EQUIPA, RESPONSABILIDADES). Advisory; the solver ignores it.

maxAlarmTableType.description: Which demand columns the alarm table consults and in what fallback order. Observed: MaxAlarmLevel_Estimate_Ideal_Minimum.

generationSequenceType.description: How the generator walks this rank. Observed: BY_LEVEL, BY_ALARM_TABLE. Not closed as an enum - SISQUAL's InpGenerationRules may carry more.

minAbilityLevel.description: Lowest-numbered (most senior) level this entry reaches.

maxAbilityLevel.description: Highest-numbered (most junior) level this entry reaches.

alarmLevelPercentage.description: Percent of the alarm level to pursue. Observed: 100.

constraints.description: Rules above the contract level. v3.0 removed this block and treated a leftover as an error; v4.0 re-admits it because SISQUAL's exporter now emits real labour-law data here (InpLabourLawCollection). Absent from the July bundle, so optional.

soft.description: Never populated in any bundle seen, so the element shape is unknown and deliberately unconstrained. Do not tighten this without a real sample.

type.description: Observed: RosterLegislation. Left open - it names which vendor rule the parameters belong to.

parameters.description: A vendor bag, deliberately open. Observed PascalCase keys: MaxConsecutiveWorkDays, MaxConsecutiveWorkDaysInWeek, MinDistanceBetweenShiftsInMinutes (all integer minutes or day counts).

startDate.description: Naive datetime YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS - a third datetime format alongside date and date-time.
